newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE wheat higher as supplies seen short.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE wheat higher as supplies seen short.

text.p: LIFFE wheat rose on a shortage of supply, despite a firmer pound, traders said.
Short covering from country and domestic buyers pushed prices higher, while a lack of farmer selling limited the amount available, one trader said.

"Farmers ain't selling a lot," he said. The tight market was also causing traders to revise down their ideas on crop size. "Crop sizes are being reviewed by the hour," he said. "Some traders are forecasting more like 14 (million tonnes of wheat), than the dizzy heights of 16." Last year's crop was 16.1 million tonnes.
On wheat, active January last traded 0.50 stg higher at 91.00 stg on volume of 302 of the total 651 lots.
Barley was mixed in thin trade, with active March down 0.25 stg at 86.25 stg on 20 of the total 37 lots.
On the basis of early cuts of wheat, the total harvest looked unlikely to be below 15 million tonnes, the HGCA said in its Weekly Bulletin, compared with the 16.1 million achieved last year.
